sanskrit: sasurāsuragandharvāḥ sayakṣoragarākṣasāḥ nālaṃ lokā raṇe jetuṃ pālyamānaṃ kirīṭinā
english: The worlds entire — with their gods, asuras, and gandharvas, with yakṣas, serpents, and rākṣasas — are not equal to conquering in battle the host guarded by the Diademed One.

sanskrit: viśvasṛg yatra govindaḥ pṛtanāris tahārjunaḥ tatra kasya balaṃ krāmed anyatra tryambakāt prabhoḥ
english: Where Govinda, maker of the universe, stands, and where Arjuna, the bane of armies, stands — whose strength could prevail there, save that of the three-eyed Lord himself?

sanskrit: satyaṃ tu te bravīmy adya naitaj jātv anyathā bhavet adyaiṣāṃ pravaraṃ vīraṃ pātayiṣye mahāratham
english: Yet truly I tell you this day, and it shall in no way prove otherwise: this very day I shall bring down the foremost hero among them, a mighty car-warrior.

sanskrit: taṃ ca vyūhaṃ vidhāsyāmi yo 'bhedyas tridaśair api yogena kena cid rājann arjunas tv apanīyatām
english: And I shall array such a battle-formation as not even the thirty gods could pierce; only, O king, by some device let Arjuna be drawn away.

sanskrit: na hy ajñātam asādhyaṃ vā tasya saṃkhye 'sti kiṃ cana tena hy upāttaṃ balavat sarvajñānam itas tataḥ
english: For in battle there is nothing unknown to him, nothing beyond his power; from this source and that he has gathered to himself all knowledge in its strength.

sanskrit: droṇena vyāhṛte tv evaṃ saṃśaptakagaṇāḥ punaḥ āhvayann arjunaṃ saṃkhye dakṣiṇām abhito diśam
english: When Droṇa had spoken thus, the bands of the Saṃśaptakas once again summoned Arjuna to battle, away toward the southern quarter.

sanskrit: tatrārjunasyātha paraiḥ sārdhaṃ samabhavad raṇaḥ tādṛśo yādṛśo nānyaḥ śruto dṛṣṭo 'pi vā kva cit
english: There a battle arose between Arjuna and the foe — such a battle as no other was ever heard of or seen anywhere.

sanskrit: tato droṇena vihito rājan vyūho vyarocata caran madhyaṃdine sūryaḥ pratapann iva durdṛśaḥ
english: Then, O king, the formation arrayed by Droṇa shone forth, hard to look upon, like the sun blazing at midday as it moves through the heavens.

sanskrit: taṃ cābhimanyur vacanāt pitur jyeṣṭhasya bhārata bibheda durbhidaṃ saṃkhye cakravyūham anekadhā
english: And at the word of his eldest uncle, O descendant of Bharata, Abhimanyu broke that wheel-formation in battle — hard though it was to pierce — in many places.

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā duṣkaraṃ karma hatvā vīrān sahasraśaḥ ṣaṭsu vīreṣu saṃsakto dauḥśāsanivaśaṃ gataḥ
english: Having wrought that deed hard to accomplish and slain heroes by the thousand, locked in combat with six warriors, he fell into the power of Duḥśāsana's son.

sanskrit: vayaṃ paramasaṃhṛṣṭāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ śokakarśitāḥ saubhadre nihate rājann avahāram akurvata
english: We were filled with utmost joy, while the Pāṇḍavas were wasted with grief; and when the son of Subhadrā was slain, O king, they withdrew from the field.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca putraṃ puruṣasiṃhasya saṃjayāprāptayauvanam raṇe vinihataṃ śrutvā bhṛśaṃ me dīryate manaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Hearing that the son of that lion among men — a boy who had not yet reached his youth, O Saṃjaya — was slain in battle, my heart is torn asunder.

sanskrit: dāruṇaḥ kṣatradharmo 'yaṃ vihito dharmakartṛbhiḥ yatra rājyepsavaḥ śūrā bāle śastram apātayan
english: Harsh indeed is this law of the warrior, ordained by the framers of duty, wherein heroes greedy for kingship let fall their weapons upon a child.

sanskrit: bālam atyantasukhinaṃ vicarantam abhītavat kṛtāstrā bahavo jaghnur brūhi gāvalgaṇe katham
english: A boy reared in utmost ease, ranging the field unafraid — how did many trained in arms strike him down? Tell me, son of Gavalgaṇa, how it came to pass.

sanskrit: bibhitsatā rathānīkaṃ saubhadreṇāmitaujasā vikrīḍitaṃ yathā saṃkhye tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: As the son of Subhadrā, of measureless might, sought to break the array of chariots and sported in the battle — tell me of that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yan māṃ pṛcchasi rājendra saubhadrasya nipātanam tat te kārtsnyena vakṣyāmi śṛṇu rājan samāhitaḥ vikrīḍitaṃ kumāreṇa yathānīkaṃ bibhitsatā
english: Saṃjaya said: That which you ask of me, O lord of kings — the felling of the son of Subhadrā — that I shall tell you in full; listen, O king, with a steady mind, how the prince sported as he sought to break the host.

sanskrit: dāvāgnyabhiparītānāṃ bhūrigulmatṛṇadrume vanaukasām ivāraṇye tvadīyānām abhūd bhayam
english: Such was the terror of your men as the terror of forest-dwellers in a wood thick with thickets, grass, and trees, when the wildfire closes about them on every side.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca samare 'tyugrakarmāṇaḥ karmabhir vyañjitaśramāḥ sakṛṣṇāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ pañca devair api durāsadāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Most fierce in their deeds in battle, their toil made manifest by their feats, the five Pāṇḍavas, with Kṛṣṇa among them, are hard to assail even by the gods.

sanskrit: sattvakarmānvayair buddhyā prakṛtyā yaśasā śriyā naiva bhūto na bhavitā kṛṣṇatulyaguṇaḥ pumān
english: In courage, in deeds, in lineage, in wisdom, in nature, in fame, and in fortune, never has there been, nor will there be, a man equal in virtues to Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: satyadharmaparo dātā viprapūjādibhir guṇaiḥ sadaiva tridivaṃ prāpto rājā kila yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Devoted to truth and duty, a giver, endowed with such virtues as reverence for the brāhmaṇas, King Yudhiṣṭhira has, they say, ever attained heaven itself.

sanskrit: yugānte cāntako rājañ jāmadagnyaś ca vīryavān raṇastho bhīmasenaś ca kathyante sadṛśās trayaḥ
english: The Ender at the close of an age, O king, the valiant son of Jamadagni, and Bhīmasena standing in battle — these three, men say, are alike.

sanskrit: pratijñākarmadakṣasya raṇe gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ upamāṃ nādhigacchāmi pārthasya sadṛśīṃ kṣitau
english: For the bearer of the Gāṇḍīva, sure to fulfil his vows in deed, in battle — for the son of Pṛthā I can find no fitting likeness upon this earth.

sanskrit: guruvātsalyam atyantaṃ naibhṛtyaṃ vinayo damaḥ nakule 'prātirūpyaṃ ca śauryaṃ ca niyatāni ṣaṭ
english: Boundless tenderness toward his elders, modesty, discipline, self-restraint, beauty beyond compare, and valour — these six are fixed firm in Nakula.

sanskrit: śrutagāmbhīryamādhuryasattvavīryaparākramaiḥ sadṛśo devayor vīraḥ sahadevaḥ kilāśvinoḥ
english: In learning, gravity, sweetness, courage, vigour, and prowess, the hero Sahadeva is, they say, the equal of the two Aśvin gods.

sanskrit: ye ca kṛṣṇe guṇāḥ sphītāḥ pāṇḍaveṣu ca ye guṇāḥ abhimanyau kilaikasthā dṛśyante guṇasaṃcayāḥ
english: All the abundant virtues that are in Kṛṣṇa, and all the virtues that are in the Pāṇḍavas — those gathered hoards of virtues, they say, are seen united in Abhimanyu alone.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirasya dhairyeṇa kṛṣṇasya caritena ca karmabhir bhīmasenasya sadṛśo bhīmakarmaṇaḥ
english: In the steadfastness of Yudhiṣṭhira, in the conduct of Kṛṣṇa, and in the deeds of Bhīmasena of terrible feats, he was their match.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayasya rūpeṇa vikrameṇa śrutena ca vinayāt sahadevasya sadṛśo nakulasya ca
english: In the beauty, the prowess, and the learning of Dhanaṃjaya, and in the modesty of Sahadeva and of Nakula, he was their equal.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca abhimanyum ahaṃ sūta saubhadram aparājitam śrotum icchāmi kārtsnyena katham āyodhane hataḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Of Abhimanyu, the unconquered son of Subhadrā, O sūta, I wish to hear in full — how was he slain upon the field of battle?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca cakravyūho mahārāja ācāryeṇābhikalpitaḥ tatra śakropamāḥ sarve rājāno viniveśitāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: The wheel-formation, great king, was devised by the preceptor, and within it were stationed kings, every one the peer of Śakra.

sanskrit: saṃghāto rājaputrāṇāṃ sarveṣām abhavat tadā kṛtābhisamayāḥ sarve suvarṇavikṛtadhvajāḥ
english: There was then a gathering of all the princes, all bound by a common compact, all with banners wrought of gold.

sanskrit: raktāmbaradharāḥ sarve sarve raktavibhūṣaṇāḥ sarve raktapatākāś ca sarve vai hemamālinaḥ
english: All clad in crimson raiment, all in crimson ornaments, all with crimson pennons, and all garlanded with gold.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ daśasahasrāṇi babhūvur dṛḍhadhanvinām pautraṃ tava puraskṛtya lakṣmaṇaṃ priyadarśanam
english: Of these firm-bowed warriors there were ten thousand, who set at their head your grandson, the fair-to-look-upon Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: anyonyasamaduḥkhās te anyonyasamasāhasāḥ anyonyaṃ spardhamānāś ca anyonyasya hite ratāḥ
english: Sharing one another's sorrows, sharing one another's daring, vying each with each, and each devoted to the welfare of the rest.

sanskrit: karṇaduḥśāsanakṛpair vṛto rājā mahārathaiḥ devarājopamaḥ śrīmāñ śvetacchatrābhisaṃvṛtaḥ cāmaravyajanākṣepair udayann iva bhāskaraḥ
english: Encircled by the great car-warriors Karṇa, Duḥśāsana, and Kṛpa, the king — like the lord of the gods, radiant, shaded by a white umbrella, fanned by the sweep of yak-tail whisks — was as the rising sun.

sanskrit: pramukhe tasya sainyasya droṇo 'vasthitanāyake sindhurājas tathātiṣṭhac chrīmān merur ivācalaḥ
english: At the front of that army, with Droṇa stationed as its commander, the lord of the Sindhus took his stand, glorious and unmoving as Mount Meru.

sanskrit: sindhurājasya pārśvasthā aśvatthāmapurogamāḥ sutās tava mahārāja triṃśat tridaśasaṃnibhāḥ
english: At the side of the lord of the Sindhus, led by Aśvatthāman, stood your sons, great king — thirty of them, like unto the gods.

sanskrit: gāndhārarājaḥ kitavaḥ śalyo bhūriśravās tathā pārśvataḥ sindhurājasya vyarājanta mahārathāḥ
english: The king of Gāndhāra, the gambler, Śalya, and Bhūriśravas — these mighty car-warriors shone forth at the flank of the lord of the Sindhus.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tad anīkam anādhṛṣyaṃ bhāradvājena rakṣitam pārthāḥ samabhyavartanta bhīmasenapurogamāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Against that host, unassailable and guarded by the son of Bharadvāja, the Pārthas advanced, with Bhīmasena at their head.

sanskrit: sātyakiś cekitānaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ kuntibhojaś ca vikrānto drupadaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: Sātyaki and Cekitāna, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the grandson of Pṛṣata, and the valiant Kuntibhoja, and Drupada the great car-warrior;

sanskrit: ārjuniḥ kṣatradharmā ca bṛhatkṣatraś ca vīryavān cedipo dhṛṣṭaketuś ca mādrīputrau ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: the son of Arjuna, and Kṣatradharman, and the valiant Bṛhatkṣatra, the lord of the Cedis, and Dhṛṣṭaketu, the two sons of Mādrī, and Ghaṭotkaca;

sanskrit: yudhāmanyuś ca vikrāntaḥ śikhaṇḍī cāparājitaḥ uttamaujāś ca durdharṣo virāṭaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: the valorous Yudhāmanyu, and the unvanquished Śikhaṇḍin, and the unyielding Uttamaujas, and Virāṭa the great car-warrior;

sanskrit: draupadeyāś ca saṃrabdhāḥ śaiśupāliś ca vīryavān kekayāś ca mahāvīryāḥ sṛñjayāś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: the sons of Draupadī in their fury, and the valiant son of Śiśupāla, and the mighty Kekayas, and the Sṛñjayas in their thousands;

sanskrit: ete cānye ca sagaṇāḥ kṛtāstrā yuddhadurmadāḥ samabhyadhāvan sahasā bhāradvājaṃ yuyutsavaḥ
english: these and others with their bands, masters of arms and frenzied for war, rushed of a sudden upon the son of Bharadvāja, eager to do battle.

sanskrit: samavetāṃs tu tān sarvān bhāradvājo 'pi vīryavān asaṃbhrāntaḥ śaraugheṇa mahatā samavārayat
english: But the valiant son of Bharadvāja, all unshaken, held back all those gathered foes with a vast flood of arrows.

sanskrit: mahaughāḥ salilasyeva girim āsādya durbhidam droṇaṃ te nābhyavartanta velām iva jalāśayāḥ
english: As great floods of water reaching a mountain hard to breach, as seas reaching the shore, they could not press past Droṇa.

sanskrit: pīḍyamānāḥ śarai rājan droṇacāpaviniḥsṛtaiḥ na śekuḥ pramukhe sthātuṃ bhāradvājasya pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Tormented, O king, by the shafts loosed from Droṇa's bow, the Pāṇḍavas could not stand before the face of the son of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: tad adbhutam apaśyāma droṇasya bhujayor balam yad enaṃ nābhyavartanta pāñcālāḥ sṛñjayaiḥ saha
english: We beheld then the marvellous strength of Droṇa's arms, in that the Pāñcālas together with the Sṛñjayas could not press past him.

sanskrit: tam āyāntam abhikruddhaṃ droṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bahudhā cintayām āsa droṇasya prativāraṇam
english: Seeing Droṇa advancing in his wrath, Yudhiṣṭhira pondered in many ways how Droṇa might be held back.

sanskrit: aśakyaṃ tu tam anyena droṇaṃ matvā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ aviṣahyaṃ guruṃ bhāraṃ saubhadre samavāsṛjat
english: Judging that Droṇa could be withstood by no other, Yudhiṣṭhira laid that heavy, unbearable burden upon the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: vāsudevād anavaraṃ phalgunāc cāmitaujasam abravīt paravīraghnam abhimanyum idaṃ vacaḥ
english: To Abhimanyu — no whit inferior to Vāsudeva, of measureless might like Phalguna, slayer of enemy heroes — he spoke these words:

sanskrit: etya no nārjuno garhed yathā tāta tathā kuru cakravyūhasya na vayaṃ vidma bhedaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: So act, dear child, that Arjuna may not return and reproach us; for we know not by any means how to break the wheel-formation.

sanskrit: tvaṃ vārjuno vā kṛṣṇo vā bhindyāt pradyumna eva vā cakravyūhaṃ mahābāho pañcamo 'nyo na vidyate
english: You, or Arjuna, or Kṛṣṇa, or Pradyumna alone could break this wheel-formation, mighty-armed one; a fifth there is none.

sanskrit: abhimanyo varaṃ tāta yācatāṃ dātum arhasi pitṝṇāṃ mātulānāṃ ca sainyānāṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ
english: O Abhimanyu, dear child, you ought to grant the boon we beg — for the sake of your fathers and your uncles and all the host alike.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayo hi nas tāta garhayed etya saṃyugāt kṣipram astraṃ samādāya droṇānīkaṃ viśātaya
english: For Dhanaṃjaya, dear child, would return from the war and reproach us; so quickly take up your weapons and shatter Droṇa's array.

sanskrit: abhimanyur uvāca droṇasya dṛḍham avyagram anīkapravaraṃ yudhi pitṝṇāṃ jayam ākāṅkṣann avagāhe bhinadmi ca
english: Abhimanyu said: Droṇa's foremost array, firm and unwavering in battle, I shall plunge into and shall break, longing for my fathers' victory.

sanskrit: upadiṣṭo hi me pitrā yogo 'nīkasya bhedane notsahe tu vinirgantum ahaṃ kasyāṃ cid āpadi
english: For the art of breaking through a battle-array was taught me by my father; but to issue forth again, should some peril arise, that I am unable to do.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bhindhy anīkaṃ yudhā śreṣṭha dvāraṃ saṃjanayasva naḥ vayaṃ tvānugamiṣyāmo yena tvaṃ tāta yāsyasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Break the array, best of warriors, and open a gateway for us; we shall follow after you, dear child, by whatever path you go.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayasamaṃ yuddhe tvāṃ vayaṃ tāta saṃyuge praṇidhāyānuyāsyāmo rakṣantaḥ sarvatomukhāḥ
english: Holding you, dear child, the equal of Dhanaṃjaya in war, we shall follow close behind you in the fray, guarding you, facing every side.

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca ahaṃ tvānugamiṣyāmi dhṛṣṭadyumno 'tha sātyakiḥ pāñcālāḥ kekayā matsyās tathā sarve prabhadrakāḥ
english: Bhīma said: I shall follow you, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and Sātyaki, the Pāñcālas, the Kekayas, the Matsyas, and all the Prabhadrakas.

sanskrit: sakṛd bhinnaṃ tvayā vyūhaṃ tatra tatra punaḥ punaḥ vayaṃ pradhvaṃsayiṣyāmo nighnamānā varān varān
english: The formation once broken by you, here and there, again and again, we shall shatter it utterly, striking down the best of their warriors one upon another.

sanskrit: abhimanyur uvāca aham etat pravekṣyāmi droṇānīkaṃ durāsadam pataṃga iva saṃkruddho jvalitaṃ jātavedasam
english: Abhimanyu said: I shall enter this unassailable array of Droṇa as a moth, all enraged, enters the blazing fire.

sanskrit: tat karmādya kariṣyāmi hitaṃ yad vaṃśayor dvayoḥ mātulasya ca yā prītir bhaviṣyati pituś ca me
english: This day I shall do that deed which serves the good of both my lineages, and which shall bring joy to my uncle and to my father.

sanskrit: śiśunaikena saṃgrāme kālyamānāni saṃghaśaḥ adya drakṣyanti bhūtāni dviṣatsainyāni vai mayā
english: This day shall all beings behold the armies of the foe driven on in their multitudes in battle by a single child — by me.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca evaṃ te bhāṣamāṇasya balaṃ saubhadra vardhatām yas tvam utsahase bhettuṃ droṇānīkaṃ sudurbhidam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: As you speak thus, son of Subhadrā, may your strength increase — you who dare to break Droṇa's array, so very hard to break;

sanskrit: rakṣitaṃ puruṣavyāghrair maheṣvāsaiḥ prahāribhiḥ sādhyarudramarutkalpair vasvagnyādityavikramaiḥ
english: guarded by tigers among men, great archers and smiters, like the Sādhyas, the Rudras, and the Maruts, with the prowess of the Vasus, of Agni, and of the Ādityas.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā sa yantāram acodayat sumitrāśvān raṇe kṣipraṃ droṇānīkāya codaya
english: Saṃjaya said: Hearing those words of his, he urged on his driver: "Sumitrā, drive the horses swiftly into battle, toward Droṇa's array!"

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca saubhadras tu vacaḥ śrutvā dharmarājasya dhīmataḥ acodayata yantāraṃ droṇānīkāya bhārata
english: Saṃjaya said: But the son of Subhadrā, having heard the word of the wise Dharma-king, urged on his driver toward Droṇa's array, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: tena saṃcodyamānas tu yāhi yāhīti sārathiḥ pratyuvāca tato rājann abhimanyum idaṃ vacaḥ
english: But the charioteer, thus urged on with "Go, go!", answered then, O king, and spoke these words to Abhimanyu:

sanskrit: atibhāro 'yam āyuṣmann āhitas tvayi pāṇḍavaiḥ saṃpradhārya kṣamaṃ buddhyā tatas tvaṃ yoddhum arhasi
english: Too heavy a burden, O long-lived one, have the Pāṇḍavas laid upon you; weigh well with your mind what is fitting, and only then ought you to fight.

sanskrit: ācāryo hi kṛtī droṇaḥ paramāstre kṛtaśramaḥ atyantasukhasaṃvṛddhas tvaṃ ca yuddhaviśāradaḥ
english: For the preceptor Droṇa is accomplished, well-practised in the highest weapons, while you have been reared in utmost ease — though you too are skilled in war.

sanskrit: tato 'bhimanyuḥ prahasan sārathiṃ vākyam abravīt sārathe ko nv ayaṃ droṇaḥ samagraṃ kṣatram eva vā
english: Then Abhimanyu, laughing, spoke these words to the charioteer: "O charioteer, who indeed is this Droṇa, or the whole warrior caste besides?

sanskrit: airāvatagataṃ śakraṃ sahāmaragaṇair aham yodhayeyaṃ raṇamukhe na me kṣatre 'dya vismayaḥ na mamaitad dviṣatsainyaṃ kalām arhati ṣoḍaśīm
english: I would do battle at the forefront of the fray with Śakra himself, mounted upon Airāvata, together with all the host of gods; this day no awe of the warrior caste is in me. This army of the foe is not worth to me a sixteenth part.

sanskrit: api viśvajitaṃ viṣṇuṃ mātulaṃ prāpya sūtaja pitaraṃ cārjunaṃ saṃkhye na bhīr mām upayāsyati
english: Having for my uncle Viṣṇu, conqueror of all, and for my father Arjuna in battle, O son of a sūta, no fear shall ever come upon me.

sanskrit: tato 'bhimanyus tāṃ vācaṃ kadarthīkṛtya sāratheḥ yāhīty evābravīd enaṃ droṇānīkāya māciram
english: Then Abhimanyu, making nothing of the charioteer's speech, said to him only, "Go, and tarry not — toward Droṇa's array!"

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃcodayām āsa hayān asya trihāyanān nātihṛṣṭamanāḥ sūto hemabhāṇḍaparicchadān
english: Then the sūta, his heart not over-glad, urged on his three-year-old steeds, decked in trappings of gold.

sanskrit: te preṣitāḥ sumitreṇa droṇānīkāya vājinaḥ droṇam abhyadravan rājan mahāvegaparākramāḥ
english: Those horses, sent on by Sumitrā toward Droṇa's array, rushed upon Droṇa, O king, with great speed and force.

sanskrit: tam udīkṣya tathāyāntaṃ sarve droṇapurogamāḥ abhyavartanta kauravyāḥ pāṇḍavāś ca tam anvayuḥ
english: Beholding him come on thus, all the Kauravas, led by Droṇa, advanced against him, and the Pāṇḍavas followed after him.

sanskrit: sa karṇikārapravarocchritadhvajaḥ; suvarṇavarmārjunir arjunād varaḥ yuyutsayā droṇamukhān mahārathān; samāsadat siṃhaśiśur yathā gajān
english: His banner raised high with a peerless karṇikāra blossom, clad in golden mail, the son of Arjuna — finer even than Arjuna — fell with eagerness for battle upon the great car-warriors led by Droṇa, as a lion's cub upon elephants.

sanskrit: te viṃśatipade yattāḥ saṃprahāraṃ pracakrire āsīd gāṅga ivāvarto muhūrtam udadher iva
english: Halting at twenty paces, intent, they joined the clash of arms; for a moment it was like the whirlpool of the Gaṅgā, like that of the ocean.

sanskrit: śūrāṇāṃ yudhyamānānāṃ nighnatām itaretaram saṃgrāmas tumulo rājan prāvartata sudāruṇaḥ
english: As the heroes fought, striking one another down, a tumultuous and most terrible battle arose, O king.
